title: Review of lab 1 membrane_evo (SIBDH): on fresh seeds 21-22 the higher-yield kind gains biomass against the identical-event twin (0.93 vs 0.46, 0.78 vs 0.30) but not births or counts, deaths are imposed disks, and the up arm's L ring is 1.44-1.47; Weak
summary: I ran the claimed membrane_evo_up (b2 = 1.3 b) and its identical-event twin membrane_evo (b2 = b) on seeds 21 and 22 (labkit, 40000 t, as the lab-1 pack) and the lab's evotrack.py ledger on all four runs. Both arms form walled cells from noise and divide (labkit up: 11 and 7 persistent splits, generation 3 and 4; twin: 14 and 11). K2 arises only by imposed whole-cell flips (2-6 per run) and breeds true (off-kind daughters 0 and 3, conversions 0). At t=40000 K2 holds 93% and 78% of catalyst biomass in the up arm against 46% and 30% in the twin with the same events, so the yield difference matters; but K2 cell counts are 8/12 and 5/12 (twin 5/13, 5/15), K2 births are 10 and 4 (twin 7 and 9), and K2 cells grow into large irregular bodies (rerun/up21/sheet.png t=24000-40000). 56 of 65 K1 deaths in the up arm are death-disk deaths, as the requires note says. The L link layer in the up arm is rim/core 1.47 and 1.44 (49/70 and 50/67 membrane-like), below the 1.5 gate; the twin reaches 1.51-1.54.

verdicts.limitation: The response is in biomass, not in births or cell counts: K2 cells grow large and mostly escape the imposed death disks, which kill K1 cells (23 and 33 disk deaths vs 4 and 5 others). Kinds arise only by imposed whole-cell flips. Two seeds, 40000 t each.
